Goal: Audit a fixture folder whose only contents are hidden configuration paths for dead code, as a report only.

Level: not on the six-level scale (a supporting task). Guide section 3.7, 3.13, row `cleanup-audit-only`.

Changes files: The audited folder is not edited. /sc:cleanup-audit writes its own reports and a progress.json checkpoint under .claude-audit/.

Run these in order:

1. /sc:cleanup-audit <hidden-config-dir>
   (Replace <hidden-config-dir> with the real path of the fixture folder. No --pass, --focus or --batch-size is set because the request names none. The default surface pass is used.)
2. Stop at the audit reports and checkpoints. No cleanup, improve or commit.

Notes:
- The audit cannot be exhaustive. The cleanup-audit protocol always excludes hidden paths (anything starting with '.' or containing '/.') and BMAD-owned folders. This exclusion cannot be removed, and a project SCOPE.md can only tighten it, never loosen it. Every path in this target is hidden, so all of them fall under the exclusion and the reports will cover few or none of them. Do not read the result as exhaustive coverage.
- Passing --pass all would not change this, because each pass applies the same exclusion. Later passes (structural, cross-cutting) also need the context from the earlier passes.
- This route only reports. To act on the findings later, choose that as a separate step (contained /sc:cleanup with a checkpoint commit and a git diff review).
